subject: Civil Engineering
title: Water in Soil: The Invisible Player
description: A quick win: understand Water in Soil: The Invisible Player.

hook.text: Add water to sand and you can build castles. Add too much and it all flows away.

buildup.text: The water table marks where soil becomes fully saturated below the surface.

discovery.text: Water pressure in soil pores pushes grains apart, reducing the soil's strength.

twist.text: Draining water from soil makes it stronger — that's why construction sites pump water out.

climax.text: Terzaghi's effective stress principle — soil strength depends on grain contact, not total weight.

punchline.text: Water makes soil soft. Remove it and the ground stands firm.

quiz.question: What does Terzaghi's effective stress principle state?
options: Soil strength increases proportionally with water content
Soil strength depends on contact forces between grains, not total weight
Deeper soil is always stronger than shallow soil
